observations: Ran the sparse GRADIENT continual update with a small budget: Adam LR 2e-2, value-only (freeze_keys=1), TF-IDF top-64 per_layer, USE_IDF=0 (pure-TF, no bg_stats), 1 epoch = 62 optimizer steps (log-confirmed: 'Sparse cache finetuning enabled: Adam (lr=0.02), top_t=64, use_idf=False', momentum_masking=freeze), GBS 32, single GH200 with gloo, from the verified Phase-1 cache on the MT synth. Authoritative dual-split eval on cache-step62.pt (mean-CE Eval loss): QA forgetting 1.6169 (n=6), MT acquisition 1.9664 (n=5); the MT value exactly matches the post-training in-training eval, confirming the correct final checkpoint. MT acquisition 1.9664 sits far below AM's closed-form ceiling 2.5426 (delta ~-0.58, well beyond the ~0.2 noise floor) and just above dense@4ep 1.87 (delta ~+0.10, near noise) and below dense@10ep 2.21 -- i.e. a few sparse gradient steps close nearly the entire AM->dense MT-acquisition gap that the closed-form value-solve could not; the in-training MT trajectory (3.78 -> 2.11 by step15 -> ~1.97 by step30, then flat to 1.966 at step62) shows the acquisition is front-loaded into the first ~15-30 steps then plateaus. QA forgetting 1.6169 is LOWER (better) than both AM 2.2521 and the Phase-1 starting cache 2.239 -- so not only no forgetting but slight positive backward transfer (caveat: tiny n=6 eval, though the ~0.6 delta exceeds the noise floor), consistent with value-only + frozen keys protecting Phase-1 while MT self-distillation over the same qasper documents reinforces shared document representations. Cost: 62 gradient steps / 689s single-GPU train wall-clock (Starting-training to cache save, incl. 6 in-training MT evals; ~708s incl. model load) -- roughly 10x the compute of AM's 0-step closed-form solve but ~1/10th of dense's 624-step budget. On the quality x cost Pareto this lands as a distinct, more-expensive-than-AM point that reaches dense-level MT acquisition and better-than-AM QA retention at ~10% of dense's gradient-step budget, dominating AM on both quality axes at modestly higher cost.
